summary: The two-step LoRA campaign survived restart, accepted four assignments and 1,024 tokens, improved held-out mean loss by 0.023848533630371094, retained 1.1036311940991158e-6 adapter relative-L2 parity, selected step 2, and produced an identity-separated release whose complete checksum inventory verified.

guardrails.detail: The coordinator was reconstructed from disk after step 1 and completed step 2 with persisted adapter, AdamW moments, cursor, history, and identities.
The final adapter relative L2 versus the centralized trajectory was 1.1036311940991158e-6, below the declared 1e-5 ceiling.
sha256sum -c verified the base, adapter, optimizer, state, data, dashboard, static worker, manifest, and every other release payload.

findings.label: Persistent adapter progress established
findings.description: Two bounded global steps accumulated into one restartable canonical adapter and improved the fixed validation use case.

findings.label: Identity-preserving adapter release established
findings.description: The release publishes the immutable base, selected adapter, optimizer moments, and full resume metadata separately while retaining explicit worker-weight and resume identities.

findings.label: Bounded local evidence only
findings.description: The corpus is a deterministic local proof fixture and workers are logical Python-oracle workers on one host, so this result does not establish remote reliability or broad model usefulness.

limitations: The positive loss change is a bounded integration signal on a small repeated local corpus, not evidence of a generally useful public model.
The evaluated release proof uses Python-oracle workers; the separate persistent browser proof covers real Burn CPU/WASM execution on the synthetic fixture.
No native-worker offload, quantization, NVMe streaming, mixed profile, or remote participant is evaluated.
